name: Daejeon
summary_text: Daejeon presents mixed evidence yielding a −0.02 deviation from the national 0.71. In October 2021 the Daejeon District Court issued Korea's most important pro-trans ruling, ordering cancellation of the Army's forced discharge of transgender soldier Byun Hee-soo and holding that the military should have considered her a woman when assessing fitness for duty—a landmark institutional recognition. In June 2024, after the Ministry of National Defense reversed the Army's 'natural death' classification and recognised her 2021 death as service-related, Byun was buried at the National Cemetery in Daejeon. Approximately 60 activists gathered to protest the burial, a visible public rejection of state recognition of a trans person at the nation's memorial ground. The court ruling is a positive institutional signal but is historical (2021) and addresses a specific administrative-military dispute rather than establishing general protections; a visitor encounters no ongoing Daejeon-specific legal advantage. The burial protest is traveler-facing (public hostility in an open space) but small in scale (60 people) and non-repeating—per the single-incident rule, it barely moves the score absent pattern. Net: the two findings largely cancel, leaving a small −0.02 below national for the residual negative event in public space. Compared to North Chungcheong (0.69), which shares the Byun case's origin but lacks the positive court ruling, Daejeon's mixed record yields the same deviation from a different direction.

sources.title: (3rd LD) Court orders cancellation of forceful discharge of deceased transgender soldier | Yonhap News Agency
sources.claim_summary: Yonhap (7 October 2021): the Daejeon District Court ordered cancellation of the Army's forced discharge of the deceased transgender soldier Byun Hee-soo, holding that the military should have considered Byun a woman when reviewing fitness for duty — described as a landmark ruling in a suit brought to repeal the discharge decision.

sources.title: Korea's first transgender soldier laid to rest at national cemetery amid controversy | Aju Press
sources.claim_summary: Aju Press (25 June 2024): Byun Hee-soo was laid to rest at the National Cemetery in Daejeon on 24 June 2024 — after the Ministry of National Defense reversed the Army's original classification and recognised the 2021 death as service-related; about 60 activists gathered to protest the burial, arguing her service did not qualify her to be interred there.

sources.title: Panel recognizes late transgender soldier as dying on-duty death | Yonhap News Agency
sources.claim_summary: Yonhap (4 April 2024): a Defense Ministry review committee recognised the late transgender soldier's death as an on-duty death, reversing the 'natural death' classification that had stood after her forcible discharge in January 2020; the ministry notified the bereaved family.
